17.0.s.en: 1. A conversation with Nathan the prophet

17.0.0.en: 1 Now it came to pass, as David sat in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, “Lo, I dwell in an house of cedars, but the ark of the covenant of the LORD remaineth under curtains.” 2 Then Nathan said unto David, “Do all that is in thine heart; for God is with thee.” 3 And it came to pass the same night, that the word of God came to Nathan, saying,

17.1.0.en: The Lord affirms that the kingdom of David and the kingdom of Solomon are merely a share in the kingdom of God Himself, for the Lord says: “I will settle him in mine house and in my kingdom for ever” [14]. In (2 Chr 9:8) the true King of Israel is God Himself.

17.1.1.en: Our Lord directed Nathan to tell David that he was not the man chosen for this work.

17.1.2.en: Now it came to pass, as David sat in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet,

17.1.3.en: “Lo, I dwell in an house of cedars, but the ark of the covenant of the LORD remaineth under curtains.” [1]

17.1.4.en: The book often repeats the prophecy of Nathan recorded in (2 Sam 7), and in its view it is of great importance. For it expresses the covenant made between God and David, and the continuity of his royal line, until the Son of David came, the eternal King.

17.1.5.en: David’s heart was aflame with love for God, so he could not bear to have a splendid palace while the ark of the covenant was placed in a tent. Therefore he wished to build a temple for the Lord. But everything has its own appointed time with the Lord. When David felt settled in the palace he had built, he wanted to build a house for the Lord in which the ark of the covenant would be placed. David’s mind was not at ease that he himself should dwell in a house of cedar while the ark was placed in a tent.

17.1.6.en: Look at David’s concern and his undertakings when his wealth increased and his power grew great. He did not think about what to do for his sons so as to share the wealth with them, or how to fill his treasuries and extend his authority, but rather he thought about what he might do to serve and glorify God.

17.1.7.en: Thus it is fitting for us to care for the service of the Kingdom of God in the world, and for His Church.

17.2.0.en: Then Nathan said unto David, “Do all that is in thine heart; for God is with thee.” [2]

17.2.1.en: As soon as Nathan the prophet learned of David’s desire, he said to him, “Do all that is in thine heart; for God is with thee,” because he had not the slightest doubt that God was with David. It is the duty of God’s servants to stir up, in themselves and in others, the movement of the grace and the gifts that are in them.

17.3.0.en: And it came to pass the same night, that the word of God came to Nathan, [3]

17.3.1.en: Some commentators (for example J. H. Blunt) see that Nathan the prophet’s advice was modified after the word of God came to him that night, since it is possible that the prophets were not always under divine inspiration, and could speak in some matters under the influence of their own human thought alone.

17.4.s.en: 2. God accompanies His people wherever they are

17.4.0.en: 4 “Go and tell David my servant, Thus saith the LORD, Thou shalt not build me an house to dwell in: 5 For I have not dwelt in an house since the day that I brought up Israel unto this day; but have gone from tent to tent, and from one tabernacle to another. 6 Wheresoever I have walked with all Israel, spake I a word to any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why have ye not built me an house of cedars?

17.4.2.en: Thus saith the LORD, Thou shalt not build me an house to dwell in: [4]

17.4.3.en: God’s answer to David’s request came thus: David does not build this house; rather he prepares for it and does not build it, just as Moses brought the people of Israel near to Canaan, but left Joshua to bring them into it. It is the right of the Lord Christ alone to be the head of His work and the one who completes it.

17.5.0.en: God condescends and accepts the good opinions of His people, even if He prevents them from carrying them out. He sent Nathan the prophet to comfort David’s heart and to say to him: 1. O David, your promotion to the high office was not in vain. I took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, not to build the temple, but to be ruler over my people Israel, and this is honor enough for you. Leave the building to another who will come after you [7]. Why should anyone think that he does everything and brings every good work to completion? Let him leave something for those who succeed him. For God gave David victories and made him a name [8], and above that He determined through him to appoint a place for His people Israel and to fortify it against its enemies; that must be his work as a man of war, and he must leave the building of churches to one who was never appointed to be a soldier. 2. O David, do not think that your good purpose has been in vain, or that you will lose its reward; for although I forbid you to carry it out, you will be rewarded as though you had done it, [for the Lord will build you an house, and will join the crown of Israel to it] [10]; for when there is a good will, it is not only accepted but also rewarded. 3. O David, do not think that I forbid you to do this great work so that it is never accomplished and that your thinking about it has been in vain; for I will raise up your seed, and he shall build me an house [11-12]. The temple of God will be built at the appointed time, even if we do not have the honor of helping to build it or the joy of seeing it completed. 4. O David, you must not confine your thoughts to the worldly prosperity of your family, but comfort yourself with the kingdom of the expected Messiah, for He is the one who comes from your loins and whose throne will be established for ever [14]. Solomon himself was not settled in the house of God as he ought to have been, and his family was not established in the kingdom: “But there shall come of your seed whom I will establish in my kingdom.” This means that he will be high priest over the house of God, and to him alone will belong authority over the works of the kingdom of God among men, and all power in heaven and on earth, in the house and in the kingdom, in the Church and in the world; so he will be a priest upon his throne, and the counsel of peace shall be between them both, and he shall build the temple of the LORD (Zech 6:12-13).

17.6.s.en: 3. God did not ask for a house for the ark, but a tent

17.6.0.en: For I have not dwelt in an house since the day that I brought up Israel unto this day; but have gone from tent to tent, and from one tabernacle to another. [5]

17.6.1.en: The time had not yet come to set the ark in a house of the Lord.

17.7.0.en: Wheresoever I have walked with all Israel, spake I a word to any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why have ye not built me an house of cedars? [6]

17.7.1.en: God does not want outward show, pomp and splendor in His service. His ark of the covenant was content with a tent, and He did not ask for a house to be built for Him, even after God had given His people rest in great and goodly cities which they built not (Deut 6:10). He commanded the judges to feed His people, but He never asked them to build Him a house [6]. May we sometimes be content with humble comforts, as the ark of God was.

17.8.s.en: 3. God’s pleasure in raising up leaders

17.8.0.en: Now therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David,

17.8.1.en: Thus saith the LORD of hosts,

17.8.2.en: I took thee from the sheepcote, even from following the sheep, that thou shouldest be ruler over my people Israel: [7]

17.9.0.en: And I have been with thee whithersoever thou hast walked, and have cut off all thine enemies from before thee, and have made thee a name like the name of the great men that are in the earth. [8]

17.9.1.en: This is God’s pleasure: to raise up every human being as a leader over his feelings, thoughts, words and conduct, so that he walks in a spirit of confidence and not of fear.

17.9.2.en: St. Cyril sees that those who do not fear God are not worthy that the psalmist should mention their names with his lips [4], but God mentions the name of the poor man with His tongue (Lk 16:19, 20) [1]. He is great in the eyes of God, and God makes him great before the heavenly beings and the sons of men.

17.10.s.en: 4. His pleasure in the rest of His people

17.10.0.en: Also I will ordain a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, and they shall be moved no more; neither shall the children of wickedness waste them any more, as at the beginning, [9]

17.11.s.en: 5. His pleasure in building a house for those He loves

17.11.0.en: 10 And since the time that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. Moreover I will subdue all thine enemies. Furthermore I tell thee that the LORD will build thee an house. 11 And it shall come to pass, when thy days be expired that thou must go to be with thy fathers, that I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall be of thy sons; and I will establish his kingdom. 12 He shall build me an house, and I will stablish his throne for ever.

17.11.1.en: And since the time that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel, I will subdue all thine enemies. Furthermore I tell thee that the LORD will build thee an house [10]

17.11.2.en: Scripture says of the two midwives who refused to kill the male children of the sons of Israel: “And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses” (Ex 1:21). Does God make houses?! Since the two midwives signify the Holy Bible, when it is studied with the fear of God and the believers live it as they ought, God establishes a place for the Scripture in many places; that is, the field of service opens and houses are raised up for God. Thus the world needs to see in us the word of God working in our heart with godly fear, so that the Gospel finds a place in every heart. Origen [2] sees in the two midwives “knowledge,” which supports the children of God in the birth of males as well as females, that is, in their having fruit in divine intellectual contemplation and in the sanctification of the emotions. For the males signify the intellect and the females the emotions. The two midwives also signify the Holy Bible with its two Testaments, Old and New, through which the children of God enjoy increasing fruit, intellectual and emotional, or spiritual and bodily.

17.12.0.en: And it shall come to pass, when thy days be expired that thou must go to be with thy fathers, that I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall be of thy sons; and I will establish his kingdom. [11]

17.13.0.en: He shall build me an house, and I will stablish his throne for ever. [12]

17.13.1.en: Although David was obliged to enter into many battles for the stability and safety of the people, the Lord did not allow him to build the temple, because his hands had shed much blood.

17.14.0.en: Who is this who builds a house for God and whose throne endures for ever, if not the Lord Christ, the Son of David, who built His Church upon the rock? Eusebius of Caesarea sees that [13] cannot apply to Solomon, but to Christ, the King of Peace.

17.14.1.en: v There is no doubt that Solomon was the son of David and his successor in the kingdom. And he was the first to build the temple of God in Jerusalem, and perhaps the Jews understand that he is the subject of the prophecy. But we rightly ask them whether the oracle applies to Solomon, which says: “I will stablish his throne for ever” [12]. And also, where did God swear with assurance by His holiness, as He foretells concerning his throne that it should be as the sun and the days of heaven?

17.14.2.en: If the years of Solomon’s reign are counted, they are forty and no more. If the years of the reign of all his descendants are added to them, they do not reach 500 years. And even if we suppose that their line (in the kingdom) continued until the last attack on the Jewish nation by the Romans, how is the prophecy fulfilled which says: “Thy throne shall remain for ever, and shall be as the sun and the days of heaven”?(*) And also the words: “I will be his father, and he shall be my son” [13].

17.14.3.en: How can they refer to Solomon? His history tells us much about him that is contrary to adoption by God and alien to it. No; hear the accusation brought against him: “But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites; of the nations concerning which the LORD said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you” (1 Kgs 11:1-2).

17.14.4.en: Add to this the saying: “And his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father. For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites. And Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD” (1 Kgs 11:4-6). Again it was said afterwards: [And the Lord raised up Satan against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite] (see 1 Kgs 11:14) LXX.

17.14.5.en: Now who can dare to say that God is the father of one who fell under such grave accusations?... Therefore we must inquire about another who is proclaimed to be of the seed of David... But there is no other born of him, as it is recorded, except our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ of God alone, who was called throughout the whole world the Son of David according to His birth in the flesh, and whose kingdom, behold, continues and will continue for ever. It has been attacked by many, but it remains always by the divine authority that surpasses humanity, to confirm that it is inspired and cannot be overcome, as the prophecy told us beforehand [3].

17.15.s.en: 6. His pleasure in His fatherhood and mercy toward us

17.15.0.en: I will be his father, and he shall be my son: and I will not take my mercy away from him, as I took it from him that was before thee: [13]

17.15.1.en: The Apostle Paul quoted this statement(**), since he understood that it is a divine promise not to Solomon the wise as a son of David who builds the temple, but a declaration concerning the Messiah, the Son of David, in whom we enjoy adoption to the Father.

17.16.s.en: 7. His pleasure in making us kings

17.16.0.en: But I will settle him in mine house and in my kingdom for ever: and his throne shall be established for evermore. [14]

17.17.0.en: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David. [15]

17.17.1.en: God gave David two promises through Nathan the prophet:

17.17.2.en: The first promise: that He will make his descendants kings of Israel [11]; this promise is conditional upon their keeping His commandments and obeying Him.

17.17.3.en: The second promise, which is unconditional: that He will raise up after him a son who will establish his throne for ever [12, 14]. This son is our Lord Jesus Christ, the incarnate Word of God, the Son of David, who establishes His kingdom in our hearts. For the Messiah in the Old Testament is the righteous eternal King, anointed to raise up the fallen tabernacle of David; His kingdom extends to the ends of the earth, and its law is truth and divine justice. Here we quote some prophecies about His wonderful person as a heavenly King and about His surpassing kingdom:

17.17.4.en: “I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth” (Jer 23:5).

17.17.5.en: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession” (Ps 2:8).

17.17.6.en: “Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre. Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows... Upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir...” (Ps 45).

17.17.7.en: “Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king’s son. He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy dwellings with truth... He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth” (Ps 72).

17.17.8.en: “And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever” (Dan 2:44).

17.17.9.en: “I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed” (Dan 7:13-14).

17.17.10.en: v When the Lord sat on the mountain with His disciples, He saw the multitudes coming to Him, so He came down from the mountain and fed them in the lower places of the mountain. For how could He have fled there again if He had not first come down from the mountain?(***)

17.17.11.en: This carries a meaning: the Lord’s descent from on high to feed the multitudes, and His ascent...

17.17.12.en: He came now not to reign immediately, but He reigns in the sense for which we pray: “Thy kingdom come.” He reigns always with the Father as the Son of God, the Word by whom all things were made. But the prophets tell us of His kingdom in which He is the Christ who became man and makes His believers Christians...

17.17.13.en: His kingdom extends and is revealed when the glory of His saints is revealed, after the judgment has been carried out by Him, the judgment of which He spoke beforehand, which the Son of Man accomplishes. Of Him the Apostle says: [when the kingdom of God is delivered to the Father] (see 1 Cor 15:24). And He Himself indicated it, saying: [Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world] (Mt 25:34).

17.17.14.en: But the disciples and the multitudes who believed in Him thought that He had come to reign at once, and therefore they wanted to take Him by force and make Him a king (Jn 6:15). They wanted to anticipate the time which He Himself had concealed in order to reveal it at the proper time [4].

17.18.s.en: 8. David offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving to God

17.18.0.en: 16 And David the king came and sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O LORD God, and what is mine house, that thou hast brought me hitherto? 17 And yet this was a small thing in thine eyes, O God; for thou hast also spoken of thy servant’s house for a great while to come, and hast regarded me according to the estate of a man of high degree, O LORD God. 18 What can David speak more to thee for the honour of thy servant? for thou knowest thy servant. 19 O LORD, for thy servant’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all this greatness, in making known all these great things. 20 O LORD, there is none like thee, neither is there any God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears. 21 And what one nation in the earth is like thy people Israel, whom God went to redeem to be his own people, to make thee a name of greatness and terribleness, by driving out nations from before thy people, whom thou hast redeemed out of Egypt? 22 For thy people Israel didst thou make thine own people for ever; and thou, LORD, becamest their God. 23 Therefore now, LORD, let the thing that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant and concerning his house be established for ever, and do as thou hast said. 24 Let it even be established, that thy name may be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel: and let the house of David thy servant be established before thee. 25 For thou, O my God, hast told thy servant that thou wilt build him an house: therefore thy servant hath found in his heart to pray before thee. 26 And now, LORD, thou art God, and hast promised this goodness unto thy servant: 27 Now therefore let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may be before thee for ever: for thou blessest, O LORD, and it shall be blessed for ever.”

17.18.1.en: I have already given an interpretation of this prayer of David in (2 Sam 7).

17.18.2.en: And David the king came and sat before the LORD, and said,

17.18.3.en: “Who am I, O LORD God, and what is mine house, that thou hast brought me hitherto? [16]

17.18.4.en: King David met God’s answer with humility [16-18], and thanksgiving [19-20], acknowledging God’s blessings [21-22], and welcoming God’s decisions, promises and commands [23-24].

17.18.5.en: David, the prophet and king, was in a state of wonderful amazement, such that no human language can express what was within him. Although God refused that David should build Him a house, David did not grieve, but rejoiced and gave thanks, because the whole discourse points to something greater than building a house for the Lord: the Lord of glory, the Son of David, comes to raise up a house which He builds with His blood shed on the Cross.

17.18.6.en: He did not feel rejected by God because He had prevented him from building a house for God; rather he felt that he was in the divine embrace, as the Father sends the Son of David to reveal practical divine love in its most wonderful form.

17.18.7.en: David’s prayer [16-27] reveals that, although he was a man with his faults, he shows his trust in God and his dependence on Him. He emphasized that the king of Israel must not rule by his own authority, but by the power of God. For he serves a people who have entered into a covenant with God and have experience of Him.

17.18.8.en: David addressed God with awe and reverence, in answer to the message of grace he had received from God; for by faith he received the promises and embraced them and was persuaded of them, as did the patriarchal fathers (Heb 11:13).

17.18.9.en: King David sat before the Lord like a little child speaking with his father, asking of Him in the spirit of sonship. For a father delights to listen to the petition of his child. He listens to him with great attention, as one who is more pleased with his words than with the words of philosophers. Thus the saint asks of God with boldness, as a son who speaks the language of love.

17.18.10.en: A child may speak few words, but by his great love for his father he speaks with boldness and abundance, because love makes it easy for him to express what is within a person.

17.18.11.en: v The child speaks before his father with love, and his father listens with love to all that he says to him.

17.18.12.en: And when he hears the questions the child puts to him, he receives them as though he were speaking about weighty matters.

17.18.13.en: Even if he prattles much and does not distinguish what he is saying, he is more pleased with his speech than with the discourse of philosophers.

17.18.14.en: Behold, I speak like a child before his father; behold, I speak before God with great love.

17.18.15.en: Behold, I speak, though very little; yet I do not speak very little, for it is easy for love to speak much, as much as it wishes [5].

17.19.0.en: And yet this was a small thing in thine eyes, O God; for thou hast also spoken of thy servant’s house for a great while to come, and hast regarded me according to the estate of a man of high degree, O LORD God. [17]

17.19.1.en: What appears in (2 Sam) as a question, “And is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?”, appears here in the form of a confession: “And hast regarded me according to the estate of a man of high degree, O LORD God.” You have made me a great man and have treated me as such. Through the covenant relationship that He grants to believers, God gives them titles, bestows gifts upon them, and prepares much for them, regarding them as persons of high rank although they are dust and ashes.

17.19.2.en: Some commentators read these words as follows: “You have looked upon me in the form of a man on high, O Lord GOD,” or “You have made me see, according to the form of man, the glory of the Lord GOD.” Therefore it refers to the Messiah, because David, like Abraham, saw His day and was glad; he saw it by faith, he saw Him in the form of a man, the incarnate Word, though he saw His glory as of the only begotten of the Father. And this is what God spoke concerning his house for a long time to come; this vision is, in God’s sight, greater than anything. It is not strange that David should speak of His humanity and His divinity: he called Him my Lord by the Spirit (divinity), although he knew that He would be his son (Ps 2:7; 110:1), and he saw Him made a little lower than the angels for a short time (humanity), but afterwards crowned with glory and honor (Heb 2:6-7).

17.19.3.en: When David heard of the two divine promises from the mouth of Nathan the prophet, he did not ask about particular details, nor about the time of their fulfillment; rather, in humility he stood before God, thanking Him and acknowledging His divine blessings.

17.20.0.en: What can David speak more to thee for the honour of thy servant? for thou knowest thy servant. [18]

17.20.1.en: After the words “What can David speak more to thee,” he added here: “for the honour of thy servant” [18]. Let us note the honor that God bestows on His servants by bringing them into a covenant and fellowship with Him, to so great a degree that they can neither speak of nor desire to be honored more than that; and if they begin to think, they cannot speak of their honor more than God has spoken.

17.20.2.en: The prophet often repeats the word “thy servant,” and does so in the name of the Son of David who emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men (Phil 2:7).

17.21.0.en: O LORD, for thy servant’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all this greatness, in making known all these great things. [19]

17.21.1.en: It is worth noting that what is stated in (2 Sam), “for thy word’s sake,” is stated here, “for thy servant’s sake” [19]; for Jesus Christ is the Word of God (Rev 19:13) and the servant of God (Isa 42:1). For His sake the promises were given to all believers, for in Him these promises become Yea and Amen. For His sake every compassion was wrought, and for His sake it was made known; we are indebted to Him for all this greatness, and from Him we expect all these things, for they are the unsearchable riches of Christ. When we look to Him by faith, and look to the hand of the Lord Christ, we cannot but glorify, not only the great things, but the one greatest thing, which is the work and riches of Christ, and speak of it with honor.

17.22.0.en: O LORD, there is none like thee, neither is there any God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears. [20]

17.23.0.en: And what one nation in the earth is like thy people Israel, whom God went to redeem to be his own people, to make thee a name of greatness and terribleness, by driving out nations from before thy people, whom thou hast redeemed out of Egypt? [21]

17.23.1.en: David the prophet recalls the Exodus that God accomplished by the hands of Moses and the signs and wonders that followed it, as a picture of God’s constant work with His people through the generations. Perhaps Ezra, as he records this prayer of David, links in the minds of his contemporaries God’s works in the Exodus of their fathers from Egypt with His work with them as they returned from the Babylonian captivity.

17.23.2.en: Those returning from the captivity after 70 years had in mind the picture of their fathers’ exodus from Egypt and their liberation from the slavery of Pharaoh.

17.24.0.en: For thy people Israel didst thou make thine own people for ever; and thou, LORD, becamest their God. [22]

17.24.1.en: How humble is David, who confesses his unworthiness, and how he magnifies the name of God and marvels at His gracious condescension, and how with piety and love he magnifies the God of Israel, and what esteem he gives to Israel’s God!

17.25.0.en: Therefore now, LORD, let the thing that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant and concerning his house be established for ever, and do as thou hast said. [23]

17.26.0.en: Let it even be established, that thy name may be magnified for ever, saying,

17.26.1.en: The LORD of hosts is the God of Israel,

17.26.2.en: even a God to Israel: and let the house of David thy servant be established before thee. [24]

17.26.3.en: In the Second Book of Samuel it is stated, “God over Israel”(****), while here it is stated, “the God of Israel,” and He is “a God to Israel” [24]. Since He is a God to Israel, this makes clear His response to the name, His establishing of the relationship, and His doing all that they need and all that they expect of Him. There were those who were called gods of the nations, such as the gods of Assyria and Egypt, and the gods of Hamath and Arpad, but they were not gods to them, because they never stood by them at all; they were merely gods in name. But the God of Israel is a God to Israel, so all His attributes and perfections overflow for their true benefit. Blessed, and thrice blessed, is the people whose God is Jehovah, for He will be a God to them with all His attributes.

17.27.0.en: For thou, O my God, hast told thy servant that thou wilt build him an house: therefore thy servant hath found in his heart to pray before thee. [25]

17.28.0.en: And now, LORD, thou art God, and hast promised this goodness unto thy servant: [26]

17.29.0.en: Now therefore let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may be before thee for ever: for thou blessest, O LORD, and it shall be blessed for ever. [27]

17.29.1.en: The closing words in (2 Sam 7) say: “And with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever,” and this is the language of holy desire, but the closing words here are the language of holy faith: [for thou blessest, O LORD, and it shall be blessed for ever] [27]. And here we see: 1. David was encouraged to ask for the blessing, because the Lord showed him that He had blessings stored up for him and for his seed: “For thou, O LORD, hast blessed me, and therefore all flesh comes to thee for the receiving of blessing; to thee I come (to receive) the blessing which thou hast promised me.” The promises were given to lead us and to stir up in us the spirit of prayer; so when God said, I will bless, let our hearts answer, Yes, Lord, bless me. 2. David was earnest in asking for the blessing, because he believed that those whom God blesses are truly blessed for ever: “Thou hast blessed, and it is blessed for ever.” Man hopes for the blessing, but God is the one who commands it; what God devises He carries out, and what He promises He does; with God, saying and doing are not two separate things. Far be it! “It is blessed for ever,” for God’s blessings are not revoked or opposed, and their benefits transcend time and days.

17.29.2.en: David ends his prayer with God’s promise of what is “for ever”; for God’s word looks to eternity, and so our desires and hopes must be.

17.29.3.en: Bless my grandchildren and my grandchildren’s grandchildren!

17.29.4.en: v David experienced Your wonderful fatherhood to him, so he longed to build You a house.

17.29.5.en: His heart found no rest after the ark of the covenant was set in the tent.

17.29.6.en: How could he rest in a palace and leave the ark in the tent?

17.29.7.en: With his pure heart, which was after Your heart, Your Spirit built a holy house in his depths.

17.29.8.en: But he was dreaming of a house for You that would befit You.

17.29.9.en: Do You, Creator of heaven and earth, dwell in houses of stone and wood?!

17.29.10.en: v Because of Your love for mankind and Your wonderful humility, You answered the request of Your beloved David.

17.29.11.en: You promised him that his son Solomon would build the house!

17.29.12.en: You counted the temple an icon of heaven and a sign of Your meeting with Your people.

17.29.13.en: v Come, O Lord Jesus, and dwell in my heart.

17.29.14.en: May Your Holy Spirit establish it, and adorn it with the spirit of holiness.

17.29.15.en: Count my heart a throne for You and a chariot like the heavenly one.

17.29.16.en: What shall I offer You that You may make Your dwelling in me?!

17.29.17.en: I have nothing to offer You but to bow down before You.

17.29.18.en: Sanctify my will, that it may be in harmony with Your will.

17.29.19.en: Lead my thoughts, my emotions and all my energy for the sake of Your Kingdom.

17.29.20.en: v To You I cry, O Lover of all mankind.

17.29.21.en: I may have children and grandchildren.

17.29.22.en: I count the whole coming generation as my children, and the generations after as my grandchildren.

17.29.23.en: I pray for the children and youth of the future.

17.29.24.en: I ask You to reveal Your love to them, that they may enter with You into a new covenant!

17.29.25.en: May they taste Your peace, Your joy and Your divine wisdom.

17.29.26.en: May they realize that You loved them before they were born!

17.29.27.en: Reveal to them Your divine presence, that they may enjoy fellowship with You.
